proposed.name: \Sigma_J
proposed.def: \Sigma_J=\{b\in[0,1]^K:b_i=0\text{ for }i\notin J,\ \sum_{i\in J}b_i=1\},\quad \operatorname{int}\Sigma_J=\{b\in\Sigma_J:b_i>0\text{ for every }i\in J\}
proposed.role: simplex of second-batch allocations supported on survivor set \(J\), with \(\operatorname{int}\Sigma_J\) denoting relative interior

proposed_core_edits.reason: The repaired unrestricted multi-survivor class requires a well-typed branch-specific survivor-allocation simplex.

proposed_core_edits.name: \mathfrak D_2^{\mathrm{all,multi}}

proposed.name: \mathfrak D_2^{\mathrm{all,multi}}
proposed.def: \mathfrak D_2^{\mathrm{all,multi}}=\bigcup_{m=2}^{K-1}\{D(\rho,a,\{b_J\}_{J\in\mathcal J_m}):0<\rho<1,\ a\in\mathcal W,\ b_J\in\operatorname{int}\Sigma_J\text{ for every }J\in\mathcal J_m\}\text{, where batch one uses }\rho a\text{, retains its top }m\text{ empirical arms, and branch }J\text{ uses }(1-\rho)b_J\text{ over its survivors}
proposed.role: unrestricted-allocation multi-survivor two-batch class for the full residual frontier

proposed_core_edits.reason: The existing class is explicitly eliminate-one-only; a distinct symbol is required for the directive's union over every survivor count and every interior first- and second-stage allocation.

proposed.name: Branch-dual saddle handle for unrestricted multi-survivor two-batch designs
proposed.construction: For each \(m\in\{2,\ldots,K-1\}\), parameterize an unrestricted two-batch top-\(m\) design by \(0<\rho<1\), an interior first-batch allocation \(a\in\mathcal W\), and a branch-specific allocation \(b_J\in\operatorname{int}\Sigma_J\) for every \(J\in\mathcal J_m\).  Thus \(D=D(\rho,a,\{b_J\}_{J\in\mathcal J_m})\in\mathfrak D_2^{\mathrm{all,multi}}\).  For a fixed tuple, replace \(q_i(\rho)\) by \(\rho a_i\), \(r_i(J;\rho)\) by \((1-\rho)b_{J,i}\), and \(n_i(J;\rho)\) by \(\rho a_i+(1-\rho)b_{J,i}\) in the survivor-set programs of \(\text{def:branch-programs}\), whose Gaussian objectives depend on the known variance vector \(s\).  This produces, for each best-exclusion or terminal branch, an explicit convex quadratic objective subject to linear inequalities.  The full-class handle jointly optimizes the resulting finite branch minimum over the discrete choice of \(m\), over \(\rho\), \(a\), and \(\{b_J\}\), and against all \(\mu\) having a unique best arm.  Its proposed optimality certificate consists of primal branch witnesses and feasible Lagrange multipliers for the branch polyhedra that give matching bounds on the robust ratio to \(I_w(\mu)\).  Neither a minimax interchange nor the value \(G_{\mathrm{multi}}\) is imposed by this definition.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The old handle optimized only eliminate-one branches.  The replacement exposes the continuous allocations and the discrete survivor-count choice in the genuinely unrestricted multi-survivor saddle problem.

proposed_core_edits.name: \Gamma_D

proposed.name: \Gamma_D
proposed.def: \Gamma_D(\mu)\text{ is the limit inferior of }-T^{-1}\text{ times the log probability that }D\in\mathfrak D_2^{\mathrm{all,multi}}\text{ deploys an arm other than }h
proposed.role: error exponent of a generic unrestricted multi-survivor two-batch design

proposed_core_edits.reason: The residual objective uses \(\Gamma_D\) for designs in the repaired multi-survivor class, so its domain must no longer be restricted to the old eliminate-one subclass.

proposed.statement:
Using the branch-dual saddle handle in \(\text{def:full-class-handle}\), characterize
\[
 \sup_{D\in\mathfrak D_2^{\mathrm{all,multi}}}
 \inf_{\mu:\,|\arg\max_i\mu_i|=1}
 \frac{\Gamma_D(\mu)}{I_w(\mu)}.
\]
Is the displayed value \(G_{\mathrm{multi}}\), or can nonproportional first-stage allocations or branch-specific survivor allocations, jointly with the discrete choice of \(m\), achieve a strictly larger certified multiplier?  Derive an attaining design and a matching saddle certificate in either case.  The restriction \(m=K-1\) is the nested unrestricted-allocation eliminate-one subquestion over \(\mathfrak D_2^{\mathrm{all}}\), not the full two-batch frontier.
proposed.justification: The unrestricted multi-survivor two-batch frontier is the genuine open content beyond the exact proportional top-\(m\) theorem.
proposed.gap: Existing batch-complexity results use different fixed-budget or fixed-confidence criteria; no cited theorem gives the joint heteroskedastic robust-gain saddle value over survivor count, first-stage allocation, and branch-specific survivor allocations.
proposed.consumer: A solution determines whether experimental platforms lose any worst-instance exponent by enforcing the proportional survivor-allocation interface and its certified discrete survivor-count choice.

obligation.what_is_open: A matching upper saddle bound for the unrestricted multi-survivor class, and hence its exact robust multiplier and an attaining nonproportional-or-proportional design, remain open.
obligation.obstruction: The feasible parameters range over the open allocation simplices and \(0<\rho<1\), and the branchwise mean adversary is coupled across every retained-set branch.  The proportional exclusion and terminal witnesses do not provide a common upper certificate for arbitrary \(a\), arbitrary \(b_J\), and every discrete \(m\); no applicable minimax interchange or uniform dual witness is present in the frozen core.
obligation.attempted: Embedded the entire proportional top-\(m\) family and reduced each fixed unrestricted design to finitely many Gaussian convex quadratic branch programs.  Branch-by-branch optimization of the adversarial mean depends on the realized allocation and does not yield one saddle witness controlling the full finite branch minimum.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The existing OEQ was mislabeled as the full frontier while ranging only over eliminate-one designs and comparing with \(G\).  This replacement makes the residual question range over all permitted survivor counts and compare with the proved proportional optimum \(G_{\mathrm{multi}}\); no proved statement is altered.

proposed_core_edits.proposed: \Gamma_{\rho,w,m}(\mu)=\min\{\min_{J\in\mathcal J_m:h\notin J}Q_J^{\mathrm E}(\rho,\mu),\min_{J\in\mathcal J_m:h\in J}\min_{j\in J\setminus\{h\}}Q_{J,j}^{\mathrm T}(\rho,\mu)\},\quad \max_{2\le m\le K-1}\sup_{0<\rho<1}\inf_{\mu:|\arg\max_i\mu_i|=1}\Gamma_{\rho,w,m}(\mu)/I_w(\mu)=G_{\mathrm{multi}},\quad \sup_{D\in\mathfrak D_2^{\mathrm{all,multi}}}\inf_{\mu:|\arg\max_i\mu_i|=1}\Gamma_D(\mu)/I_w(\mu)\stackrel{?}{=}G_{\mathrm{multi}}
proposed_core_edits.reason: The metadata must distinguish the proved proportional multi-survivor optimum from the residual unrestricted multi-survivor saddle question.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Prove or refute \(\sup_{D\in\mathfrak D_2^{\mathrm{all,multi}}}\inf_{\mu:\,|\arg\max_i\mu_i|=1}\Gamma_D(\mu)/I_w(\mu)=G_{\mathrm{multi}}\), and exhibit an attaining design with a matching saddle certificate.
open_obligations.obstruction: The finite quadratic branch programs are explicit for each fixed design, but arbitrary first-stage and branch-specific survivor allocations couple the least-favorable mean across all retained-set branches.  The frozen results provide no allocation-uniform dual witness and no minimax interchange over the open simplices and the discrete choice of \(m\).
open_obligations.attempted: Used \(a=w\) and \(b_{J,i}=w_i/W_J\) to embed every proportional top-\(m\) design and obtain the lower bound \(G_{\mathrm{multi}}\).  Also substituted general \(a\) and \(b_J\) into the Gaussian polyhedral branch programs.  Optimizing a witness separately for each branch does not furnish a single mean vector adversarial for the full branch minimum.

prose_updates.honest_scope: The exact exponent, top-\(m\) projection inequality, matching survivor-set witnesses, timing optimum, discrete optimization over \(m\), equal-variance reduction, and rounded Chernoff certificate are proved for independent Gaussian streams with known finite positive variances and a unique best arm. The old eliminate-one result is the \(m=K-1\) reduction. The genuinely unrestricted residual class is now \(\mathfrak D_2^{\mathrm{all,multi}}\): it jointly ranges over the survivor count, every interior first-batch allocation, and every branch-specific interior survivor allocation. The proved proportional family embeds in this class and certifies a lower bound of \(G_{\mathrm{multi}}\), but a matching allocation-uniform upper saddle certificate is open. The former unrestricted-allocation eliminate-one class \(\mathfrak D_2^{\mathrm{all}}\) remains only the nested \(m=K-1\) subquestion. Unknown-variance adaptation, non-Gaussian rewards, variance ratios changing with budget, \(K=2\), and finite-sample risk dominance are outside the theorem.
